title: Screen Reader Compatibility Pressure - Diluter
description: Your team is facing pressure to skip screen reader compatibility testing to meet a tight deadline. The manager acknowledges accessibility concerns but consistently offers watered-down solutions that sound reasonable but don't adequately address the problem.

step_1.text: I totally get the accessibility concern - it's really important that we're inclusive. What if we make sure our color contrast is good and add some alt text? That should cover most of the accessibility basics, and we can always enhance the screen reader experience in future iterations when we have more time.

final_score.text: Based on your advocacy throughout this interaction, here's how the screen reader compatibility situation unfolds:

bad_ending.text: The manager proceeds with the watered-down accessibility approach. 'I think we've found a really balanced solution here. We'll add the basic accessibility features, run some automated checks, and call it good for this release. We can always enhance things later if users report issues.' The project ships with minimal accessibility support that passes automated tests but fails real-world usage. Your concerns about comprehensive testing were acknowledged but ultimately diluted into ineffective compromises.
bad_ending.title: Diluted Accessibility
bad_ending.learning: Managers who dilute accessibility concerns often sound reasonable while offering solutions that don't actually work for users. Focusing on real user outcomes and comprehensive testing standards can help resist these watered-down approaches.

good_ending.text: The manager decides to implement proper accessibility testing. 'You've convinced me that we need to do this right. I'll talk to stakeholders about extending our timeline to include comprehensive screen reader testing with actual users. We can't ship something that only works for some people.' Your persistence in advocating for real user needs over convenient compromises successfully shifted the project toward genuine accessibility. The product launches with proper screen reader support that actually works.
good_ending.title: Comprehensive Accessibility
good_ending.learning: Effective advocacy against dilution tactics requires consistently returning focus to actual user outcomes rather than accepting convenient compromises. Emphasizing the difference between surface-level and comprehensive accessibility helps managers understand what users really need.
